title: How much does a business phone system cost?
summary: Business phone costs range from $10 to $65+/user/mo. Learn what drives pricing, common add-on charges to watch, and how Zoom Phone can help you get more value.
body_markdown:
If you've ever Googled "business phone system cost" and come away more confused than when you started, you're not alone. The answer depends on what kind of system you choose, how many people need it, and — crucially — what's actually included in the price. Cloud-based voice over internet protocol (VoIP) systems have changed the math dramatically, putting enterprise-grade calling within reach of even the smallest teams, but hidden fees and add-ons can quickly erase those savings if you don't know what to look for.

## The 3 types of business phone systems (and what each costs)


Not all business phone systems are built the same — and your choice will have the biggest impact on what you pay, both upfront and every month.


### Traditional landline / on-premises PBX


A private branch exchange (PBX) is the classic office phone setup: hardware installed on-site, physical handsets, and calls routed over the public telephone network (PSTN). It's reliable, but the cost of entry is steep.


- **Upfront hardware and installation:** $5,000–$20,000+ for a typical small-to-midsize deployment — before ongoing maintenance
- **Monthly per-line costs:** $35–$70/line, plus separate charges for long distance
- **Maintenance contracts:** $1,000–$3,000/year on average


For businesses with a few dozen employees, an on-premises PBX can easily run into six figures over its lifetime — and it doesn't travel with your team.


### Hosted VoIP (cloud-based)


A hosted VoIP system routes calls over the internet instead of copper wire. There's no on-site hardware to buy or maintain, and pricing is per user per month. Generally, prices for business VoIP range from roughly $10/user/month for basic service to $40+/user/month for advanced solutions — with most small businesses landing around $20/user/month.


The savings compared to traditional systems are significant.[Independent cost analysis](https://www.invisionaz.com/feeds/blog/voip-business-phone-system-cost) shows cloud VoIP typically costs 37–41% less than traditional PBX over a five-year period.


### Unified communications as a service (UCaaS)


UCaaS goes further than a standalone VoIP line. It bundles calling with video meetings, chat, SMS, and often AI-powered features — all in one platform. For teams that currently pay separately for a phone system, a video conferencing tool, and a messaging app, consolidating into a single UCaaS platform can cut the total cost of ownership significantly.


System type Upfront cost Monthly cost per user Best for


**Traditional PBX** $5,000–$20,000+ $35–$70/line Static office environments


**Hosted VoIP** $0–$500 (hardware optional) $10–$40 Remote/hybrid teams


**UCaaS** $0 $16–$50+ Teams wanting calling + meetings + chat in one place


## What factors affect the cost of a business phone system?


Even within the same category, prices vary widely. Here's what often drives the number up or down:


- **Number of users.** Most cloud plans are priced per seat. The more people you add, the more you pay — though many providers offer volume discounts.
- **Calling plan type.** Metered (pay-as-you-go) plans cost less per month but charge per minute. Unlimited domestic plans may cost more upfront but deliver predictable bills if your team makes frequent calls.
- **Features and add-ons.** Auto-attendants, call queues, analytics dashboards, and AI features are often bundled with higher tiers — or sold separately as add-ons. Read the fine print.
- **International calling.** Domestic unlimited plans don't cover international calls. If your team calls internationally with any regularity, expect to add $10/user/month or more, or choose a global plan.
- **Hardware.** Softphone apps (desktop and mobile) are free. Physical desk phones typically run $50–$300 per device. Many businesses skip desk phones entirely.
- **Contract length.** Annual billing typically reduces the monthly rate by 10–25% compared to month-to-month plans.


## Common add-on charges to watch out for


Sticker price and actual price aren't always the same. Common add-on charges that can inflate your bill:


- **SMS and MMS fees.** Some providers charge per text message or require a separate messaging add-on. Look for plans that include domestic SMS and MMS at no extra cost.
- **E911 fees.** Emergency services routing compliance sometimes appears as a separate monthly line item.
- **Number porting fees.** Moving your existing business number to a new provider can cost $10–$50 per number, depending on the provider.
- **Compliance and recording fees.** Call recording, storage, and regulatory compliance tools are often priced as add-ons.
- **Setup and onboarding fees.** Some legacy providers charge for initial configuration. Cloud-first systems typically have no setup fee.


When comparing providers, build a complete per-user cost that includes all the features your team actually needs — not just the base plan rate.


## How much does a cloud VoIP system cost per user?


Here's a quick-reference breakdown of what you can expect to pay by tier:


Tier Typical cost/user/month What's usually included


**Entry-level (metered)** $10–$20 Pay-as-you-go calling, basic call handling, voicemail


**Mid-tier (unlimited domestic)** $20–$30 Unlimited US/Canada calling, SMS, call recording, integrations


**Advanced / UCaaS** $30–$40+ Calling + video + chat + AI features, analytics, global calling


Keep in mind: two providers at the same price point can include very different feature sets. AI-powered call summaries, voicemail transcription, and built-in integrations with CRM and other business tools are increasingly standard on mid-tier and above — but not universal.

## Security and compliance costs — a factor many buyers overlook


Many cost guides focus on per-user pricing and feature tiers. What they often overlook is the cost of meeting compliance requirements and maintaining security — and that can be a significant gap for businesses evaluating their options.


For many businesses that handle sensitive customer calls, operate in a regulated industry, or simply need to meet E911 requirements, security and compliance aren't optional. With some providers, meeting those requirements may mean layering on third-party tools or paying for compliance add-ons.


Zoom Phone includes features to support security and compliance requirements, including E911 support to help businesses stay prepared for emergency situations. Role-based access controls enable admins to manage who can see call logs, recordings, and settings without needing deep technical expertise. For a full overview of Zoom's certifications and attestations visit our[Compliance at Zoom](https://www.zoom.com/en/trust/legal-compliance/) page.


## How to calculate the true cost of a business phone system


The monthly per-user rate is just the starting point. A true total cost of ownership (TCO) calculation should factor in:


1. **Monthly recurring costs** — per-user plan fee × number of seats
2. **Add-ons** — international calling, compliance tools, recording storage, AI features (if not bundled)
3. **Hardware** — desk phones, headsets (optional with softphone-first systems)
4. **Setup and training** — one-time costs; cloud systems are typically self-serve
5. **Displaced tools** — what you can cancel when calling, video, and chat consolidate onto one platform


That last point is where[cloud phone systems](https://www.zoom.com/en/blog/what-is-voip/) often deliver the clearest return. Managing multiple carriers and legacy systems can drive up costs and complexity.


For a 10-person team currently paying separately for a phone system ($20/user), a video tool ($15/user), and a chat app ($10/user), consolidating onto a single UCaaS platform at $20.50/user could cut that stack cost significantly while adding capabilities — like AI call summaries and voicemail prioritization — that weren't there before.


## Frequently asked questions


### What is the average cost of a VoIP phone system for a small business?


The average small business target is around $20/user/month, with most small businesses paying between $10 and $40 per user per month for a cloud VoIP system, depending on the plan tier and features included.


### Is VoIP cheaper than a traditional phone system?


Yes, in most cases — significantly so. Traditional on-premises PBX systems often require $5,000–$20,000 or more in upfront hardware and installation, plus ongoing maintenance contracts. Cloud VoIP has no upfront hardware cost.


### Are there hidden fees with business phone systems?


There can be. Common extras include SMS/MMS charges, E911 fees, number porting fees, call recording storage, and compliance add-ons. When evaluating providers, always ask for a fully loaded per-user cost that includes the features your team actually needs.


### What is included in a business phone plan?


It varies by provider and tier. A standard cloud VoIP plan typically includes inbound and outbound calling, a business phone number, voicemail, and basic call management (hold, transfer, call routing). Mid-tier and above often add unlimited domestic calling, SMS, call recording, and integrations. UCaaS bundles like Zoom Phone add video meetings, chat, and AI-powered features like call summaries and voicemail prioritization.


### Can I keep my existing business phone number when switching?


Yes. Most cloud VoIP providers support number porting — transferring your existing business number to the new system. You can bring over company phone numbers from your old system without service interruptions. Check with your new provider for porting timelines, which typically run five to 10 business days.


### What is the cheapest business phone system?


The cheapest cloud VoIP entry point is typically a metered (pay-as-you-go) plan, which runs around $10–$12/user/month. Zoom Phone offers a metered plan that includes calling, SMS, voicemail, AI features, and integrations — making it a capable entry-level option. Note that metered plans charge per minute for outbound calls, so they work best for light callers with low messaging volume.
